statementSummary: I build and evaluate AI systems that must work reliably outside the lab. My work spans a deployed real-time traffic perception system (YOLOv8 with multi-object tracking), LLM-based applications and multi-agent pipelines. I am interested in how to measure whether such systems can be trusted: how detection errors propagate into decisions, how efficiently models can run on modest hardware, and when LLM agents and vision-language models can replace or complement purpose-built pipelines in low-resource, heterogeneous settings.

researchInterests.summary: Detection and tracking for heterogeneous traffic, with attention to model size, inference latency, and how detection errors affect downstream congestion decisions. Evidence: final-year project using YOLOv8n and ByteTrack, with 89.5% validation and 89.1% held-out test mAP@50.

Role-specialized multi-agent LLM pipelines with tool calling, and how to measure their reliability against single-agent baselines. Evidence: Podcaster Crew, a CrewAI pipeline with researcher, reporting-analyst and scriptwriter agents using web search and Gemini speech synthesis (https://github.com/MuhammadAwais-32013/podcaster_crew); LangChain and Model Context Protocol research-report generator; LangGraph project; Hugging Face MCP certificate.

Domain-specific question answering with retrieval-augmented generation, and measuring groundedness and hallucination. Evidence: DiaBP Diet Consultant, a mobile and web health assistant with a FastAPI RAG backend (Gemini, FAISS, Sentence Transformers) and OCR for medical documents; ArticleSift uses LLaMA 3.1 and Google Custom Search for live-news question answering. Formal RAG evaluation is in progress.

Speech synthesis, prompt engineering, and multilingual applications. Evidence: Gemini text-to-speech podcast generation in Podcaster Crew; ArticleSift audio narration and translation into English, Urdu, Spanish, and French; and eighth place at a national Generative AI hackathon.

fypDetails.title: Real-Time Traffic Choking Point Detector
fypDetails.status: Final Year Project, NUML Islamabad (completed 2026). Held-out evaluation is complete; a vision-language-model comparison is in progress.
fypDetails.abstract: This project develops a real-time congestion monitoring system for two Islamabad junctions (NUML Gate and 7-Up Chowk). A YOLOv8n detector, fine-tuned on a self-collected four-class traffic dataset, is combined with ByteTrack and count-based congestion rules. Alerts are served through a FastAPI backend to a React dashboard and SMS. Validation results are 89.5% mAP@50, 59.3% mAP@50-95, 86.4% precision, and 84.7% recall. On a held-out test set of 162 images and 799 instances, the detector reaches 89.1% mAP@50, 54.8% mAP@50-95, 82.2% precision, and 86.8% recall. Inference was measured at 3.1–5.7 ms per image on a Tesla T4.

results.split: Validation split (used to select the best epoch); separate held-out test split contains 162 images and 799 instances.
results.efficiency: 3.1–5.7 ms per image on a Tesla T4; model size 6.3 MB.
results.training: 282 epochs (best epoch 232), about 2.7 hours, COCO-pretrained initialization.

limitations: Metrics are from the validation split; an independent test set from different days or viewpoints is still needed.
At the confusion-matrix threshold, vehicle predictions exceed ground truth by roughly 23%, and the human class has low precision (many false positives, possibly unlabeled objects).
Congestion is decided by a fixed vehicle-count threshold rather than learned from speed, occupancy or stop duration.
Data come from two junctions, so cross-site generalization is untested.
All vehicle types are merged into a single class.

dataset.name: NUML Junction Traffic Dataset (working name)
dataset.size: 1,642 images and 6,612 labeled objects; 80/10/10 train/validation/test split.

methodology.detail: Collected traffic data at NUML Gate and 7-Up Chowk in Islamabad.
Annotated 1,642 images and 6,612 objects across vehicle, bus, human, and traffic-controller classes.
Fine-tuned YOLOv8n for 282 epochs, with the best checkpoint at epoch 232; training took about 2.7 hours on a cloud GPU.
Added ByteTrack for persistent IDs and applied count-based rules to raise congestion alerts.
Served alerts through a FastAPI backend to a React dashboard and SMS.

openQuestions: How do per-frame detection errors, such as the observed vehicle over-counting, propagate into congestion-state decisions, and can tracker-derived features (occupancy, speed, stop duration) replace fixed count thresholds?
When can open-weight vision-language models complement or replace a fine-tuned detector for congestion-state classification in heterogeneous traffic, and at what latency and cost?
How do multi-agent LLM pipelines compare with single-prompt baselines on citation correctness and unsupported claims?
How can the groundedness of retrieval-augmented health and nutrition assistants be measured, and how often do they produce unsupported claims compared with a no-retrieval baseline?
